summary: Subaccount invoice shows one-off rate override after org migration
description: Issue summary: After completing an org-to-org migration on 2026-03-11, Docstream Health reports that one of their subaccounts received an unexpected rate override on its hourly usage lines. The rate shown on the invoice is higher than the legacy rate the subaccount had prior to migration. Customer believes pricing should have carried over unchanged for committed reserved capacity and asks for immediate correction and a credit if overbilled.
impact: Customer-facing billing discrepancy affecting month-to-date charges for a production org. Potential revenue impact ~USD 12k if not corrected. Customer has paused sending non-critical batch jobs until resolved.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer initiated org migration via Console on 2026-03-11 (migration-id: mig-20260311-docstream).
2) Post-migration, subaccount 'docstream-analytics' started to receive usage attribution under new org id.
3) Billing export for 2026-03-11 to 2026-03-12 shows hourly lines with 'rate_override=true' and unit_price higher than pre-migration rate tier.
4) Customer compared pre-migration invoice (Feb 2026) and post-migration draft invoice (Mar 2026) and identified delta on reserved GPU hourly lines.
5) Customer opened support ticket requesting investigation and provisional credit.
logs: metering-raw: metering/us-east/2026-03-11/usage-logs.gz (sample lines show rate_override flag)
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 10:15Z - Support ingested customer's draft invoice and identified that 'docstream-analytics' had a different rate_key (rate_key: rsv-2025-q4-v2) post migration compared to pre-migration (rate_key: rsv-2025-q3).
2026-03-12 11:02Z - Billing team pulled migration audit trail; migration recorded a 'rate_policy_bind' event for the subaccount that was unexpected and lacks operator justification.

2026-03-12 13:40Z - Metering service shows an intermediate state where usage was attributed to parent org for a 45-minute window; a backfill job re-attributed usage to subaccount and applied current org's default pricing (which differs from legacy reserved pricing).

Hypothesis: the migration path triggered a default-pricing fallback for subaccounts that did not have a pinned rate_key in the new org. The backfill re-attribution applied new org defaults rather than preserving legacy reserved commitments.
Evidence: rows in metering export include 'backfill=true' and 'applied_rate_key=default-dedicated-2026' for timestamps between 03:15 - 04:00 UTC on 2026-03-11.
Immediate risk: invoices already drafted for period include these lines; if billing pipeline is not corrected a larger monthly invoice will be generated at month close.
Requested artifacts: full migration audit, backfill job id, pre/post rate_key mapping for subaccount, and raw metering lines for affected hour window.

Ravi Menon 2026-03-13T16:40Z: PR#4123 merged to alter backfill pricing behavior. Plan: re-run backfill with preserve_legacy_rate flag and generate corrected invoice lines. Scheduled re-run 2026-03-14 02:00Z.

Priya Kapoor 2026-03-14T08:10Z: Re-run completed. Preliminary reconciliation shows corrected delta USD -7,150 (credit owed to customer). Preparing final credit memo and updated invoice draft. Will close after customer confirmation.
resolution: Action taken: Billing ops issued provisional credit (USD 6,800) on 2026-03-13. Metering infra fixed backfill behavior (PR#4123) and re-ran backfill on 2026-03-14; final reconciliation indicates a total credit of USD 7,150. Final credit memo and corrected invoice draft generated and shared with customer. Follow-up: create migration runbook step to preserve rate_key during org transfers and add an automated test to block backfills that would override pinned pricing. Ticket to remain open until runbook created and customer sign-off received.
next_steps: Finalize and send credit memo and corrected invoice to Docstream (owner: Priya).
Document migration runbook update and add to Confluence (owner: Ravi).
Add automated integration test to CI to prevent future backfills from applying default pricing when migration header exists (owner: Metering infra).
Monitor Docstream billing for one full billing cycle and confirm no further anomalies (owner: Support).
